Preparing for an AI-first career and rapid fire

takeaways: Mark Smith runs a nine-agent AI software factory in which each agent fills one gated role in the DevOps loop, from requirements and architecture to coding, security, release and documentation.
Owning the agent harness with OpenClaw keeps context and data in his own Azure environment, so models from different providers can be swapped without rebuilding the system.
For an AI-first career, Mark recommends moving from prompt engineering to context and outcomes engineering, learning about harnesses and avoiding lock-in to a single vendor.
hook: What happens when AI agents become the whole software team? Mirko Peters talks with Mark Smith (NZ365Guy) about his OpenClaw-based AI software factory, Ralph loops, governance and why context engineering matters more than prompts. A practical look ahead for developers, consultants and IT leaders preparing for AI-first software engineering.
